author: Cosmas Mogere
title: More Than 140 Wisconsin Workers Face Job Losses as Tomahawk and Marshfield Plant Closures Raise Questions About Local Manufacturing Future - NewsBreak
text:
By Cosmas Mogere ,
9 hours ago Image Credits:Ramon FVelasquez, CC BY-SA 3.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
Two Wisconsin communities are preparing for a difficult transition after separate manufacturing facilities in Tomahawk and Marshfield announced closures that are expected to eliminate more than 140 jobs , creating uncertainty for workers, families, and local economies.
The closures highlight the challenges facing smaller communities that have long depended on manufacturing employers for stable jobs and economic activity. While the companies involved cited business decisions behind the moves, the impact extends beyond factory floors, affecting suppliers, local businesses, and residents who rely on manufacturing employment.
In Marshfield, the planned closure of a Foremost Farms facility is expected to affect 68 employees , according to reports on the company’s announcement. In Tomahawk, a separate manufacturing plant closure is expected to impact approximately 76 workers , according to local reporting.
Together, the closures represent a significant employment disruption for communities where manufacturing has historically played an important role.
Marshfield Workers Face Loss of Longstanding Manufacturing Jobs Image Credits:Wikideas1, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons
The Marshfield closure involves Foremost Farms , which announced plans to shut down its local facility. The company’s decision is expected to eliminate 68 positions , with the closure timeline reported for mid-December.
Foremost Farms, a dairy cooperative serving farmers across the Midwest, has operated processing facilities as part of its broader agricultural supply chain. The Marshfield shutdown reflects changes within the company’s operations and comes as manufacturers nationwide continue to evaluate production costs, efficiency, and market conditions.
For affected employees, the closure represents more than a workplace change.
Manufacturing jobs often provide long-term employment opportunities , support household incomes, and contribute to community stability. When a major employer closes, restaurants, retailers, service providers, and other businesses that depend on local workers can feel the effects.
Local officials and workforce agencies typically respond to closures by connecting displaced employees with retraining programs, unemployment resources, and new employment opportunities.

Tomahawk Closure Adds to Regional Employment Concerns In Tomahawk, another manufacturing facility closure is expected to affect approximately 76 workers , according to local reports.
The announcement adds another employment challenge for a northern Wisconsin community where manufacturing has been part of the local economic foundation.
While details surrounding the Tomahawk closure continue to develop, workforce officials often emphasize the importance of early assistance for workers facing layoffs. Programs may include career counseling, skills assessments, and support in finding new positions.
For smaller communities, losing dozens of jobs can have an outsized impact because manufacturing employers often represent a significant share of available career opportunities.
Related: 9 Career Regrets People Often Have After 40 and the Lessons They Wish They Learned Earlier
Why Manufacturing Closures Matter Beyond the Factory Manufacturing plants frequently serve as economic anchors . They provide direct employment and support transportation companies, maintenance services, suppliers, and local businesses.
When a facility closes, the immediate concern is usually the workers affected. However, economists note that secondary effects can emerge if displaced employees reduce spending or if suppliers lose business.
The impact depends on several factors, including how quickly workers find new employment, whether other employers are hiring, and whether new investment enters the community.
For communities such as Marshfield and Tomahawk, the response often involves balancing short-term support for affected workers with longer-term efforts to attract new businesses.
A Changing Manufacturing Landscape The Wisconsin manufacturing sector has experienced ongoing changes as companies adjust to shifting consumer demand, technology investments, and operating costs.
Some manufacturers have expanded through automation and modernization, while others have consolidated operations or moved production as part of broader business strategies.
Industry analysts say manufacturing remains a major part of Wisconsin’s economy, but individual communities can experience significant disruption when a single employer closes.
The recent closures in Tomahawk and Marshfield do not establish a statewide trend on their own, but they reflect the challenges communities face when traditional employers restructure operations.
Workers and Communities Look Ahead For employees affected by the closures, the coming months will likely involve difficult decisions about employment, training, and financial planning.
Workforce development agencies often encourage workers to begin exploring options before final layoffs occur, including updating resumes, identifying transferable skills, and connecting with employers seeking experienced workers.
Meanwhile, community leaders may focus on attracting new investment and supporting existing businesses that can help offset job losses.
The closures also renew broader questions about how smaller Wisconsin communities can maintain economic stability as industries evolve.
The Next Chapter for Tomahawk and Marshfield The loss of more than 140 manufacturing positions is a significant moment for both communities, but local economies often adapt through periods of change.
New employers, workforce programs, and business development efforts can influence how quickly communities recover from major job losses.
For now, workers and families in Tomahawk and Marshfield are focused on the immediate impact: understanding the timeline, exploring options, and preparing for what comes next.
The closures remind us that behind every manufacturing announcement are employees, families, and communities whose futures are directly tied to decisions made inside corporate offices and factory walls.
